Polish Istanbul Today

Consulate General of Poland in Istanbul

From Jagiełło's first envoys in 1414 to the secret wartime base 'Bey' of 1940–41: more than six centuries of Polish diplomacy on the Bosphorus now have an address in Maslak.

Theme
Polish Istanbul Today
District
Sarıyer (Maslak)
Period
1414–
Visiting
Limited access

The story

Polish diplomacy has more than six hundred years of history on the Bosphorus – and its address today is the consulate general in a Maslak office tower.

The count starts in 1414: according to the chronicle of Jan Długosz, the envoys of King Władysław Jagiełło, Jakub Skarbek of Góra and Grzegorz the Armenian, were received that year by Sultan Mehmed I, most likely at Bursa – Constantinople was still a Byzantine city. The two countries marked the 600th anniversary in 2014, when Presidents Bronisław Komorowski and Abdullah Gül opened a major exhibition at Istanbul's Sakıp Sabancı Museum.

How to visit

Address: Maslak Mah., Eski Büyükdere Cad. 7, GİZ 2000 Plaza, 5th floor, Sarıyer. Maslak is on the M2 metro line – check the nearest station in your map app. It is an office, not a sight: consular visits are by appointment, and opening hours and the emergency duty phone are listed on gov.pl/web/turcja (the consulate does not answer questions by e-mail and refers to its website).
